title: TrustFoundry Benchmarks — suite manifest
description: Declares a suite at suites/<id>/suite.json: its identity, publication status, and the targets it can run. This document describes the shape; nothing in the package loads it to validate against — the enforcement lives in src/core/suites.mjs, and test/suites.test.mjs asserts the two stay in agreement. See ../../../docs/adapter-contracts.md.

id.description: Must match the manifest's own directory name, suites/<id>/.

status.description: published suites appear in the generated README tables; experimental and deprecated do not.

targets.description: Keyed by target id, e.g. suites/<id>/targets/<targetId>. A target's config triple must resolve to real files under configs/.

additionalProperties.$comment: A resolved target also carries a `bundle` field equal to its own key — the directory leaf a published result bundle lives under. It is derived by the loader, not authored here: this schema has no `bundle` property, and `additionalProperties: false` means a manifest that tries to set one is rejected as an unknown key.

benchmark.description: Repo-relative path to the benchmark config, e.g. configs/benchmarks/<suite>/<name>.json.

provider.description: Repo-relative path to the provider config, e.g. configs/providers/<name>.json.

scorer.description: Repo-relative path to the scorer config, e.g. configs/scorers/<name>.json.

rows.description: Row count the target's benchmark config is expected to produce — a sanity bound, not the source of truth for row count.

headline.description: Whether this target's result is the one surfaced as the suite's headline number.

tier.description: smoke targets are cheap sanity runs; full targets are the publication-grade run.
